changes.old: Широкий участок декодирования изображения в профиле рабочего процесса
changes.new: ### Reading a sampled flame graph A sampling profiler periodically records the call stack of a thread. A flame graph groups these observations by call path. A wide frame appeared in many retained stacks; it does not mean that the function was called that many times. One long invocation may appear in many samples, while a short invocation can occur between samples and be missed. ![[02 Areas/ML & DL/00 Учебник/Assets/Figures/curated/profiling-2026-11-04/py-spy-flamegraph.svg|Original inverted py-spy flame graph: calculate_similar_artists branches into fit and similar_items, with argpartition and _wrapfunc nested below the similarity-score calculation]] *Ben Frederickson, [py-spy — record](https://github.com/benfred/py-spy/blob/7a7ac96e96e0f9b4ba3eee80de3f4d255698170b/README.md#record). Complete original SVG, 1200×182, with its original labels and sample counts. [MIT license](/licenses/py-spy-7a7ac96e-MIT.txt). No crop, redraw or relabeling. Enlarge the figure to read the frames. The original SVG's hover details and frame zoom are available when opening its file.* The root is at the top in this **inverted** layout; following a branch downwards follows nested calls. The `all` frame represents 2893 retained samples. At the `calculate_similar_artists` level, the location `lastfm.py:79` accounts for 1490 samples, or 51.50% of the total. The location `lastfm.py:95` accounts for 1371 samples, or 47.39%. The wide branches identify where to inspect the calling code; the picture alone does not explain why those paths dominate. The counts in the original SVG also show why parent and child widths cannot be added as independent work: | Nested frame | Samples | |---|---:| | `_get_similarity_score`, line 209 | 814 | | its `argpartition` child | 813 | | that child's `_wrapfunc` child | 813 | The 813 observations in `argpartition` already belong to the 814 observations of its parent. The same 813 stacks continue into `_wrapfunc`. Adding 814, 813 and 813 would count most of those observations three times. The source percentages are 28.14%, 28.10% and 28.10% of the same 2893 samples, not three disjoint shares of execution. The frame coordinates are rounded for drawing; use the recorded counts rather than measuring pixel widths. Horizontal position is not chronology. For an illustrative capture that includes idle stacks, let `D` mean decoding and `W` mean waiting. The observed sequences `[D,D,D,D,D,D,W,W]` and `[D,D,D,W,D,D,D,W]` both contain six decoding and two waiting samples. Their aggregate widths are identical, although the waits occur at different points. A flame graph cannot recover that order. A timeline retains event order and is needed to relate a wait to a particular missing batch or CUDA launch. Brendan Gregg explains this distinction in [Flame Graphs, Summary and Variations](https://www.brendangregg.com/flamegraphs.html#Summary). The denominator depends on what the profiler retains. With `--idle`, `py-spy` includes stacks it would otherwise classify as idle. With `--gil`, it retains only stacks holding the GIL and can omit work in native extensions that release it. With `--subprocesses`, worker processes contribute their own stacks. Compare profiles with the same capture options, and inspect which process or thread each branch belongs to. These options and their limitations are documented in the pinned [py-spy FAQ](https://github.com/benfred/py-spy/blob/7a7ac96e96e0f9b4ba3eee80de3f4d255698170b/README.md#frequently-asked-questions). This is the source repository's recommender-system example, not a fresh measurement of our model or DataLoader. Its counts establish what this picture contains; they do not establish a GPU bottleneck, elapsed seconds or an expected speedup. Широкий участок декодирования изображения в профиле рабочего процесса
